t: Further Report On The Documents In French Obtained By The Local Japanese Consular Police

pages.en:
N.K.
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S. 2. Special Branch Station,
REPORT
Date May 13 1936
Subject (in full) Further report on the documents in French obtained by
the local Japanese Consular Police.
Made by D. S. Kamashita Forwarded by
With reference to my previous report dated April 30,
1936 concerning the documents in French obtained by the local
Japanese Consular Police, I have to state that the documents,
according to the Consular Police, were sent by post to the
staff of a local Japanese shipping concern on or about April
10 and were subsequently submitted to the Consular Police.
The Japanese Consular Police, however, have declined to disclose
the names of the staff and the Japanese shipping company in
question. It is stated that the staff is at present absent
from Shanghai on leave.
D. Kamashita
D. S.
Officer i/c, Special Branch.
（左侧批注：J.B.R. / Bn / FILE）
（右上角印章/文字：MUNICIPAL / File No. REGIST / D.）

S. 2. 特务科分署，
报告
日期：1936年5月13日
主题（全称）：关于当地日本领事馆警察所获法文文件的进一步报告。
制作人：D. S. Kamashita 转呈人：
兹提及本人于1936年4月30日提交的关于当地日本领事馆警察所获法文文件的先前报告，现须说明，据领事馆警察称，这些文件于4月10日左右通过邮寄方式发送给当地一家日本航运公司的工作人员，随后被提交给领事馆警察。然而，日本领事馆警察拒绝透露该工作人员及涉事日本航运公司的名称。据悉，该工作人员目前休假不在上海。
D. Kamashita
D. S.
特务科主管警官。
（左侧批注：J.B.R. / Bn / 归档）
（右上角印章/文字：MUNICIPAL / 档案号 REGIST / D.）

SECRET
202-d
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No: REGIST
B. D.
Section 2, Special Branch
REPORT
Date May 2, 1936
Subject Anti-Japanese documents obtained by Japanese Consular Police.
Made by D. S. Jones Forwarded by L. S. S.
In the report by D.S. Kamashita no mention is made as
to where the documents in French, photostatic copies and
translations of which are attached, bearing on the self-styled
"World League against Conquest and Colonisation," were obtained
by the local Japanese Consular Police, but the latter have
been approached re this point and it is hoped that further
enlightenment will shortly be forthcoming. There is nothing
in Police records concerning such a League, nor is there any
information available regarding the person named Vansang to
whom the letter dated March 4, 1936 is apparently addressed.
At first sight the letter in question appears to have
been written in Shanghai and addressed to "Vansang, 198 Avenue
de Paris, Chatillon-sous-Bagneux (Seine)", the heading at top
left of letter. This is supported by the fact that under the
date at the top right hand corner of the letter appear the
words "Shanghai, China." However, perusal of the last
paragraph inclines one to the belief that instead of the letter
having been written in China and sent to France, the reverse
actually took place, the author of the letter being Vansang,
the self-styled President-Founder of the "World League against
Conquest and Colonisation", who seems to be corresponding with
a collaborator living in Shanghai. This last paragraph, which
stresses the need for adherents "in all countries, especially
in China" would hardly appear in a letter sent from China to
some other country. Then again; the membership form leaves
a space for signature after "Shanghai", which clearly indicates
that the form was intended for subscribers living in this city.
The final injunction to return the completed form to Mr. Vansang,
the President-Founder, who resides at Chatillon-sous-Bagneux,

档案号：REGIST
B. D.
特务科第二股
报告
日期：1936年5月2日
主题：日本领事馆警察查获的反日文件。
制作人：D. S. Jones 转呈人：L. S. S.
在 D.S. Kamashita 的报告中，并未提及当地日本领事馆警察是从何处获得那些附有影印副本及译文的法文文件的，这些文件涉及自称的“世界反征服与反殖民联盟”。已就此点向后者进行查询，期望不久能获得进一步说明。警方档案中并无关于此类联盟的记录，也没有关于名为 Vansang 之人的任何信息，而1936年3月4日的信件显然是写给此人的。
乍看之下，涉案信件似乎是在上海撰写，并寄往“Vansang, 198 Avenue de Paris, Chatillon-sous-Bagneux (Seine)”，即信件左上角的抬头地址。信件右上角日期下方出现的“Shanghai, China.”字样也佐证了这一点。然而，细读最后一段使人倾向于认为，事实并非信件从中国写往法国，而是恰恰相反；信件的作者是 Vansang，即自称的“世界反征服与反殖民联盟”主席兼创始人，他似乎正与一名居住在上海的合作者通信。这最后一段强调了在“所有国家，尤其是中国”拥有追随者的必要性，这种内容几乎不会出现在从中国寄往其他国家的信件中。此外，会员申请表在“上海”之后留有签名空格，这清楚地表明该表格是供居住在本市的订阅者使用的。最后要求将填妥的表格寄回居住在 Chatillon-sous-Bagneux 的主席兼创始人 Vansang 先生，

would remove all remaining doubt as to the origin of the
letter were the stamped addressed envelope (in which one
presumes the documents to have been sent) available for
examination, which is not the case. The Japanese authorities
could clear up this point by informing the Shanghai Municipal
Police how the documents came into their possession.

It therefore seems clear from the photostatic copies of
the documents already supplied by the Japanese Consular Police
that the man calling himself Vansang is a person residing in
France out to make capital from the anti-Japanese element in
Shanghai. He may be a genuine pro-communist working on behalf
of the so-called "World League against Conquest and Colonisation",
or simply an opportunist choosing what appears to be an easy
way of making money.

The Japanese authorities request that they be furnished
with any information obtained in connection with these
documents. However, beyond inquiries already conducted into
this affair little more can be done until we learn something
of the circumstances under which the Japanese obtained
possession of the said documents.

JBR
2/26

secure further information

若能查验贴有邮票并注明地址的信封（推测文件是通过该信封寄送的），便可消除关于信件来源的所有剩余疑点，但事实并非如此。若日方能告知上海公共租界工部局警务处这些文件是如何落入他们手中的，即可澄清此点。

因此，从日本领事馆警察已提供的文件影印副本来看，情况似乎很明确：那个自称 Vansang 的人是一个居住在法国、企图利用上海反日分子牟利的人。他可能是一名真正的亲共分子，代表所谓的“世界反征服与反殖民联盟”开展工作，或者仅仅是一个投机分子，选择了一条看似轻松的赚钱途径。

日方要求向其提供与这些文件有关的任何已获信息。然而，除了已经对此事进行的调查外，在我们了解日方获得上述文件的具体情况之前，很难再做更多工作。

JBR
2/26

C. D. I. Ross
出示给 D.S. Kamashita
并询问他能否
获取更多关于
来源的信息。
HR    S. 2.

L. Jones
D. S.

特务科主管警官。    JBR 1936年5月4日
